# Patches carried on top of llama.cpp

<!-- GENERATED by `python3 .github/check-patches.py --render` from llama/patches/*.patch -- do not edit;
     the code-style job fails when this page is stale. -->

Every native library this project ships is built from the pinned llama.cpp source with the patches
below applied, in this order (`llama/cmake/apply-llama-patches.cmake`). They are the difference
between a java-llama.cpp binary and upstream's: bug fixes upstream has not merged yet, and the
embedding glue a JVM needs that upstream will not carry. Each is submitted upstream where it is
upstream-shaped, and dropped here the moment upstream carries the fix (the drop-checks are in
`CLAUDE.md`, "Local llama.cpp source patches"). Every natives jar names the ids it was built with
in its `jllama-build.txt` (`patches=`) and a hash over the set (`patches.sha256=`), so a consumer can
match a binary to this page.

**36 patches.** Ids as `jllama-build.txt` lists them under `patches=`.

## 0002-server-preserve-caller-load-progress-callback.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server-context.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: keep a load-progress callback the embedding caller installed

Since b9789 server_context::load_model unconditionally installs the server's own load-progress
reporter on params_base.load_progress_callback right before common_init_from_params, clobbering the
callback an embedding caller set -- libjllama wires LoadProgressCallback to a JNI trampoline before
load_model, so Java saw no progress and the abort-on-false path never fired. The guard installs the
server's reporter only when no callback is set OR when the one set is the server's own: load_model
runs a second time on wake from the sleeping state (--sleep-idle-seconds), and a bare nullptr check
would then leave user_data pointing at the dead stack frame of the first call (segfault on the
first request after an idle window). Standalone llama-server is unaffected.

Drop-check on every bump: read the load-progress assignments in server_context_impl::load_model()
(tools/server/server-context.cpp) -- once upstream keeps a callback the caller set and still
re-points its own reporter's user data at the current frame on every load (a second load runs when
the server wakes from the idle sleep), drop the patch; until then it is needed, and the guard is
LoadProgressCallbackTest plus CApiSleep.AWakeDoesNotCallTheLoadProgressCallbackAgain.
```

## 0003-pr22393-server-add-slot-prompt-similarity-getter-setter.patch

**Files (2):** `tools/server/server-context.cpp`, `tools/server/server-context.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
Upstream PR: ggml-org/llama.cpp#22393 — "server : add slot_prompt_similarity getter/setter"
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22393

Carried locally until the PR is merged upstream. Adds public get/set accessors for the
server_context `slot_prompt_similarity` field so an embedding/JNI caller can query and tune
the slot-selection threshold at runtime without reloading the model. The change is purely
additive (two new accessors + their declarations) and is a verbatim copy of the upstream PR,
so it can be dropped from patches/ once b<nnnn> includes it. Refresh against the new source on
every llama.cpp version bump (the applier fails loud if the context shifts).

Update: upstream closed PR #22393 without merging -- ngxson rejected it, reasoning that
slot_prompt_similarity is internal, single-use-case state that shouldn't be exposed as public
API and should instead live in downstream code. This patch is therefore now carried
indefinitely, not pending-merge; it will never be droppable via an upstream bump and must keep
being refreshed on every version bump.

Refreshed at b12387: upstream added server_context::set_video_decoder() where the two
declarations sat; only context moved, the + lines are unchanged.

Refreshed at b12416: upstream #32154 moved slot selection into server_slot_sched, so the
threshold is impl->slot_sched.slot_prompt_similarity now. It is set from
params_base.slot_prompt_similarity at the same place of load_model() as before; the accessors
read and write that member instead. This applied cleanly and failed to compile -- the applier
cannot see a member that moved.
```

## 0006-server-embed-native-server-jni.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: make llama_server() embeddable in a host process (no signal handlers, stoppable)

b9870 exposes int llama_server(int, char **) with no main() in server.cpp; this patch adds what a
JVM host needs to run it inside libjllama: a g_llama_server_embedded flag with
llama_server_set_embedded() / llama_server_request_shutdown() (declared by the host in
native_server_bridge.h), no process-wide SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers in embedded mode (they would
hijack the JVM's), and a shutdown handler guarded by g_shutdown_handler_mutex and reset before the
locals it captures are destroyed -- a request landing after llama_server() returned used to run the
lambda over destroyed objects (SIGSEGV in server_http_context::stop(), seen in router mode).
Runnable guard: src/test/cpp/test_native_server_shutdown.cpp.

Refreshed at b11881: #31113 split llama_server() into one function per role (server_run_router,
server_run_instance, server_run_download) and added server_run_opts. The embedded mode now clears
server_run_opts::install_signal_handlers (upstream's own switch, which llama-cli uses) instead of
guarding the sigaction block, and each role function that installs a shutdown handler declares the
reset after the last local its handler captures: models_routes in the router, ctx_http in the
instance.

Refreshed at b12014: #31417 removed the Windows argv reconstruction from common_params_parse (the
defect 0001 carried a fix for, dropped at the same bump), so the forwarded-argv hunk is gone:
llama_server() calls common_params_parse for every caller, and it parses the argv it is given.

Refreshed at b12316: #31467 made the download progress throttle per file and added
`#include <mutex>` (and <unordered_map>) to server.cpp itself, so the hunk that added the include
for g_shutdown_handler_mutex is gone. 6 hunks: the flag, the guarded handler, the two resets, and
opts.install_signal_handlers.

Since the review of 2026-11-18 the embedded server also skips the common_log_flush() at the end of
llama_server(): it pauses and resumes common_log's worker without the engine's g_common_log_mutex,
and the host's setLogger / log-file changes take that lock.

Since round three of that review the patch also adds llama_server_parsed(params, argc, argv): the
same server over an argv the embedding host has parsed already. NativeServer's engine parses the
argv once, under its log lock, to refuse a bad argv at the start and to own the log file; a second
parse inside llama_server() read every file option again, and one from a pipe (--api-key-file
/dev/stdin) the second time empty -- the server then ran without its API key. llama_server_parsed()
does not call common_init(): the host calls it before its parse, as llama_server() does, since
2026-11-19 -- called after the parse it turned common_log's prefix and timestamps on again, so
--no-log-prefix / --no-log-timestamps had no effect (CApiLogFile.TheLogPrefixAndTimestampOptionsOfTheArgvTakeEffect).

Refreshed at b12637: #32398 serves /models/sse on a single-model server too, so
server_run_instance's shutdown handler also stops the SSE clients (sse_stopping, a local declared
before ctx_http like the others it captures); the hunk that guards it moved with it.

Drop-check on every bump: none of this is upstream's yet. Read tools/server/server.cpp for an
embedded mode of its own (no process signal handlers, an out-of-band shutdown, a parse the caller
does) -- once it has one, port native_server.cpp to it and drop the patch.
```

## 0007-server-attach-http-frontend.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: let an embedding host attach the HTTP frontend to an already-loaded server_context

Adds llama_server_attach(argc, argv, server_context &, server_routes &), which serves a model the
host has already loaded over the upstream HTTP frontend: no second model load, no start_loop() --
the host's worker keeps driving the shared server_context and the HTTP routes post tasks to its
queue. The attach entry point registers upstream's own server_register_routes() (the route table and
the GCP shim) plus the instance (non-router) resumable-streaming handlers through
server_register_stream_routes(), exactly what server_run_instance() registers, so the two entry
points cannot drift on the endpoint set; it answers /cors-proxy and /tools with 403 (the MCP/tools
host belongs to a full llama-server), marks ready immediately and blocks in ctx_http.join() until
llama_server_request_shutdown(). It serves the caller's server_routes rather than a frame-local one:
server_routes' constructor registers a sleeping-state callback on the model's task queue that
outlives the attach call. Applies after 0006 (and builds only with it: it uses 0006's
shutdown-handler functions).

Refreshed at b11881: #31113 factored the route table out of llama_server() itself
(server_register_routes, server_register_stream_routes), so the patch no longer extracts a copy of
it -- the helper this patch used to add, and the "verbatim copy" invariant it had to keep, are gone.

Since the review of 2026-11-18 the patch also adds llama_server_attach_parsed(params, ...), the attach
entry over an argv the host has parsed already (see 0006's llama_server_parsed: one parse, so a file
option from a pipe is read once).

Drop-check on every bump: read tools/server/server.cpp for an entry point that serves the HTTP
routes over a server_context the caller loaded -- once upstream has one, port the attach mode to it
and drop the patch.
```

## 0008-server-models-worker-cmd-override.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server-models.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: let the router spawn its model workers through a host-supplied command (LLAMA_SERVER_WORKER_CMD)

The router (server-models.cpp) starts each model worker by re-executing its own binary
(get_server_exec_path(): /proc/self/exe and friends). Inside a JVM that binary is java, not a
llama-server, so embedded router workers could never start. The environment variable
LLAMA_SERVER_WORKER_CMD (whitespace-split, read in server_model_meta::update_args) replaces the
leading binary-path token of the rendered worker command, so a host relaunches workers through its
own bootstrap -- here `java -cp app.jar net.ladenthin.llama.server.NativeServer`, set from Java by
NativeServer.setWorkerCommand(). Also useful for containerised or wrapped deployments.

Drop-check on every bump: read server_model_meta::update_args in tools/server/server-models.cpp --
once the worker command can be replaced without re-executing the router's own binary (an option or
an environment variable of upstream's), use that and drop the patch.
```

## 0014-common-log-callback-sink.patch

**Files (2):** `common/log.cpp`, `common/log.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
common: add a callback sink to common_log (common_log_set_callback)

An embedding host (here: the java-llama.cpp JNI binding) has no way to receive the
lines that common_log prints: llama_log_set() covers only llama/ggml, while the
server's SRV_*/SLT_* macros write straight into common_log and end up on stderr no
matter what the host configured. common_log offers file, colors, prefix, timestamps,
verbosity and JSONL, but no hook.

This adds common_log_set_callback(log, cb, user_data): while set, the worker thread
hands every entry to the callback instead of printing it (a file set via
common_log_set_file still receives it). The callback gets the formatted message
without prefix/timestamp/colors and has the ggml_log_callback signature, so one
function can serve both llama_log_set() and this sink. Swapping the callback pauses
the worker first, so entries already queued reach the previous sink.

Upstream-submittable ("common : add a callback sink to common_log for embedding
hosts"); not yet filed. Guarded by src/test/cpp/test_common_log_callback.cpp.

Drop-check on every bump: `grep -n "common_log_set_.*callback\|set_callback" common/log.h` at the
new tag. On upstream without this patch the grep returns nothing (common/log.h names only
common_log_default_callback, which a plain `grep callback` finds either way); a hit is upstream's
own sink -- port setLogger to it and drop the patch.
```

## 0015-rpc-embeddable-client-and-stoppable-server.patch

**Files (5):** `common/arg.cpp`, `ggml/include/ggml-rpc.h`, `ggml/src/ggml-rpc/ggml-rpc.cpp`, `ggml/src/ggml-rpc/transport.cpp`, `ggml/src/ggml-rpc/transport.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-rpc: let an embedding host register servers and stop its own server safely

An embedding host (here: the java-llama.cpp JNI binding, which runs llama.cpp inside a
JVM) cannot use ggml-rpc as it is:

1. A registration that fails is an error. Upstream answers an unreachable or malformed endpoint
   and a failed handshake with a nullptr since b12283 (#30415; until then this patch carried that
   half, see "Reduced at b12283" below); add_rpc_devices() (common/arg.cpp) registered that nullptr
   silently and ran without the requested server. It now throws std::invalid_argument naming the
   server.

   A server that vanishes mid-run stays fatal: the paths after registration (buffer, graph and
   tensor calls) abort through RPC_STATUS_ASSERT when a send fails. That includes
   ggml_backend_rpc_get_device_count() for an endpoint whose dispatcher a still-open model keeps
   alive (get_dispatcher() reuses it): a second load of a server that died while the first model on
   it is still open ends the process in the host's re-check below. It needs a real error path
   through the backend interface.

2. add_server() returns a cached registration without checking that the server is still
   there, so re-using an endpoint whose server had stopped passed registration and aborted
   on the first tensor upload. ggml_backend_rpc_get_device_count() -- which asks the server
   and answers 0 when it cannot be reached -- is now in the backend's proc-address table, and
   the host asks it for an endpoint it registered before (rpc_support.hpp, register_server).
   Until the review of 2026-11-19 the patch re-checked the cache hit inside add_server()
   itself; that connected to the server again on every --rpc the parse saw, under whatever
   lock the caller held -- the engine parses under the lock of the process-wide log, so a slow
   server stalled every logger swap and every other load for as long as its connect took.

   ggml_backend_rpc_get_device_memory() of a server that went away reports 0/0 (upstream's own
   behaviour since b12283), which matters because registered devices stay in ggml's process-wide
   registry forever and code that never uses them still queries their memory: common_init() lists
   every device at -lv 4, and --list-devices does too. ggml_backend_rpc_init() aborts by name when
   the registration of a reachable server fails.

3. ggml_backend_rpc_start_server() cannot be stopped: while(true) around accept(). Two new
   entry points, both also exposed through get_proc_address:
   - ggml_backend_rpc_stop_server() disconnects the client and every live peer socket.
     Listener accept and outgoing peer connect poll cancellation at 50 ms intervals; no
     wake-up connection can fill the listen backlog and block the stopping thread. The
     loop releases its backends when it ends.
   - ggml_backend_rpc_server_listening() tells the host whether the socket was bound.
   The transport stays initialised on the way out, because WSACleanup() would invalidate
   every other RPC socket in the process.

4. transport: no SIGPIPE when the peer went away (MSG_NOSIGNAL / SO_NOSIGPIPE), a
   socket_t::shutdown() (on Windows also CancelIoEx: shutdown alone does not wake a recv
   blocked in another thread there), and the file descriptors that connect()/create_server()/accept()
   leaked on their error paths are closed.

Upstream-submittable; not filed upstream yet. The runnable guard is
src/test/cpp/test_rpc.cpp: it links both new functions and exercises the registration and
stop paths over loopback. test_rpc_comm.cpp drives protocol-v10 COMM_INIT through the C
API: loopback/network binding, missing peer, stalled caps handshakes in both ranks,
normal peer setup, socket cleanup and restart. Subprocess deadlines bound failures.

5. COMM_INIT preserves the configured server bind address instead of opening a wildcard
   listener for a loopback-only server. Peer sockets are weakly registered before any
   caps I/O, under the same mutex as stop; stop also catches a peer accepted/connected
   concurrently. Normal COMM_FREE/disconnect still frees them immediately. The rank-1
   retry loop checks cancellation too. The former main-listener wake-up connection is
   removed: repeated C-API stops while the peer was absent filled its backlog.

Drop-check on each upstream bump: inspect comm_init, the stoppable accept/connect
paths and stop_server. Drop upstream-fixed hunks instead of mechanically refreshing them.

Refreshed at b12079 (#28967, NCCL for multi-node tensor parallelism): COMM_INIT accepts
world-1 peers on rank 0 instead of one (comm_state::peers, a vector in rank order), factors
the capability exchange into comm_caps_handshake(), has every peer send its rank after it, and
negotiates the communicator over those sockets (comm_bootstrap_exchange) before it answers.
The cancellation contract is carried over unchanged: every accept of the loop and the
connect/retry of a higher rank observe the stop flag, and each peer socket is registered with
rpc_server_track_peer() before its first blocking read, so a stop shuts it down under the
mutex wherever COMM_INIT blocks on it -- the handshake, the rank, or the bootstrap exchange.
Not covered: a backend communicator's own init (ggml_backend_comm_init_rank, CUDA with NCCL)
blocks inside the backend until every rank has joined and has no cancellation.

Refreshed at b12217 (#29413, "RPC: Improve loading times", protocol 9.0.0): the HELLO answer
carries server feature flags and negotiate_hello() takes the dispatcher's flags to fill; the
hunk that turns a failed handshake of rpc_dispatcher::start() into a reported failure is
rewritten over that call. Nothing else moved.

Reduced at b12283 (#30415, "ggml-rpc : fail gracefully on unreachable endpoints and failed
handshakes"): upstream took the client half -- rpc_dispatcher::start() returns false instead of
aborting, negotiate_hello() reports a failed exchange, get_dispatcher() returns nullptr and does
not cache a failed attempt, and every consumer answers nullptr conservatively (device memory
0/0, device count 0). Those hunks are dropped, with this patch's try_get_dispatcher() /
aborting get_dispatcher() pair. What stays of the client: the device count in the proc-address
table, with which the host re-checks an endpoint registered earlier (upstream returns the cached
registration of a server that has gone away), and ggml_backend_rpc_init() aborts by name when the
registration of a reachable server fails. The server half (stop, listening, COMM_INIT bind
address and cancellation, transport) is unchanged.

Refreshed at b12387 ("ggml : prune", protocol 10.0.0): upstream reformatted the
declaration of ggml_backend_rpc_start_server() in ggml-rpc.h over several lines, the context
of the hunk that declares the stop and listening functions after it. Only context moved; the
+ and - lines are unchanged, 24 hunks.

Refreshed at b12658 (#32651, "rpc : typed request helpers and a single validation step on the
server"): upstream moved every fixed-size command to typed helpers and one validation step,
which shifted the server's code by some 200 lines and split one hunk in two. The + and - lines
are unchanged; the wire format is too (protocol 10.0.2), so a client and a server of b12657
and b12658 still speak to each other.

Refreshed at b12683 (#32896, "rpc : reuse one context for request tensors on the server"): the
server's constructor creates that context after the vectors it sizes, the trailing context of
the hunk that adds the bind address to the constructor. Only context moved; the + and - lines
are unchanged, and so is the wire format.
```

## 0017-ggml-cpu-x86-prefetch-byte-offset-and-msvc-type.patch

**Files (2):** `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/prefetch.h`, `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu(x86): byte-wise prefetch address, and a type clang accepts on MSVC targets

The four _mm_prefetch calls in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c (the SSSE3-without-AVX
branch of ggml_vec_dot_q4_0_q8_0) carry two independent defects. Both are fixed by routing the
address through one new static inline helper, ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/prefetch.h; the call
sites change from a raw expression to ggml_prefetch_at(&x[ib], sizeof(block_q4_0)) and nothing
else moves. The helper is header-only and included relatively, so no CMake change is needed.

1. Type -- this breaks the build on a current clang. MSVC declares the intrinsic as
   `void _mm_prefetch(char const *, int)`. Clang's own xmmintrin.h defines a macro that casts to
   `const void *`, but it sits behind `#ifndef _MSC_VER`: on a *-windows-msvc target clang leaves
   the declaration to Microsoft. Passing `const block_q4_0 *` is then
   -Wincompatible-pointer-types, which clang 22 promoted to an error by default (llvm-project
   #157364; the 22.1.0 release notes say "The -Wincompatible-pointer-types diagnostic now
   defaults to an error; it can still be downgraded to a warning by passing
   -Wno-error=incompatible-pointer-types"). NOT clang 16 -- an earlier version of this header
   claimed that, but clang 16 promoted only -Wincompatible-FUNCTION-pointer-types.

   Measured on the real file at -msse4.2, plain clang (the GNU driver, which
   cmake/x64-windows-llvm.cmake selects) on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, before and after this patch:

     clang 20.1.8   unpatched -> 4 warnings, object file produced   patched -> 0 errors, 0 warnings
     clang 22.1.3   unpatched -> 4 errors,   no object file         patched -> 0 errors, 0 warnings
     clang 23.1.3   unpatched -> 4 errors,   no object file         patched -> 0 errors, 0 warnings

   (20.1.8 and 23.1.3 locally with MSVC 14.44.35207 headers; 20.1.8 and 22.1.3 on a
   windows-2025-vs2026 runner, which carries both.) The practical consequence is that
   -DGGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON cannot be built
   with a current plain clang on Windows, because the `sse42` variant compiles this branch: ggml
   passes it -msse4.2 (its `/arch:` branch is behind `if (MSVC)`, false for plain clang), which
   defines __SSSE3__ without __AVX__ and so selects `#elif defined(__SSSE3__)`. It is the only
   such variant -- the x86-64 baseline (`x64`) has no SSSE3 and takes the scalar branch, and
   every richer variant has AVX. -msse4.2 -mavx builds for that reason. clang-cl and MSVC are
   unaffected (the macro and the warning level differ), as is clang on a GNU target.

2. Arithmetic -- wrong on every platform, including where the call compiles.
   `&x[ib] + sizeof(block_q4_0)` adds sizeof() *elements*, not bytes. With the sizes that
   ggml-common.h pins by static_assert (block_q4_0 == 18, block_q8_0 == 34) the prefetch targets
   +324 and +1156 bytes instead of +18 and +34, and the "+ 2 *" pair targets +648 instead of
   +36 -- 18 and 34 times too far. The call sites plainly intend "the next block" and "two blocks
   ahead", which is what byte-wise arithmetic gives. Measured: no throughput difference on a
   Ryzen 7 5800H forced onto the sse42 kernel with a 0.6B Q4_0 model (pp512 101.3 vs 100.9,
   tg128 37.3 vs 37.0, both inside the other's error bars), so this is a correctness fix, not a
   performance one; a genuine SSE4.2-era machine was not available to measure.

Upstream-submittable, and intended to be submitted: the fix is confined to one new header plus
four call sites and changes no behaviour beyond the prefetch address.

Why upstream's own build is green -- measured, and no longer an open question. Their windows-cpu
release job builds exactly this with plain clang, GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS=ON and no suppressing
flag (CMAKE_ARGS carries only build-target toggles), and ships ggml-cpu-sse42.dll. The reason it
works is the clang version: the windows-2025-vs2026 image has LLVM 20.1.8 on PATH, where these
are warnings. Note how narrow that is -- the same image also ships clang 22.1.3 inside Visual
Studio 2026 (VC/Tools/Llvm/x64), which fails on the unpatched file; upstream reaches the working
one only because C:\Program Files/LLVM/bin comes first on PATH. It was NOT a header difference
-- all three MSVC toolsets on that image
(14.29.30133, 14.44.35207, 14.51.36231) declare _mm_prefetch identically as
`extern void _mm_prefetch(char const*_A, int _Sel);`, which was the first hypothesis and is
disproved. So this patch is ahead of upstream rather than diverging from it: their build breaks
the moment the runner image ships a clang that makes the diagnostic fatal, and until then they
compile four warnings and a prefetch address that is 18x/34x too far.

At b12525 (#32548, upstream's CI moved to LLVM 22.1.8) upstream took exactly that form:
`(const char *) (&x[ib] + sizeof(block_q4_0))` on all four calls -- the type half is fixed upstream
now, the address is still 18x/34x too far. The patch was refreshed onto those lines (only the `-`
side changed) and keeps both halves through ggml_prefetch_at.

Runnable guards: src/test/cpp/test_prefetch.cpp drives ggml_prefetch_at against the real
block_q4_0 / block_q8_0 types and asserts the offsets are byte-wise -- the helper only, red when the
helper is written element-wise or with the cast around the whole expression. That the four call
sites of quants.c go through the helper is checked by llama/cmake/check-prefetch-byte-offset.cmake,
which fails the configure on every platform when a _mm_prefetch call of the patched file does not
(upstream's `(const char *)(&x[ib] + sizeof(block_q4_0))` compiles and keeps (2), so a refresh that
lost the quants.c hunks would pass every other check).

On a bump, check whether upstream fixed this themselves:
`git grep -n _mm_prefetch ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/x86/quants.c` in the new tag. That grep is a
LOCATOR, NOT A VERDICT -- it returns FOUR hits at every tag, because the calls exist either way
(measured at b11639 (a0e6dc738): lines 846, 847, 864, 865). Read them: the fix is upstream's only
when the cast to a byte pointer happens BEFORE the addition. `(const char *)(&x[ib] + sizeof(...))`
casts the whole expression, silences the compiler and keeps the wrong address, so it looks fixed and
is not -- reading the four calls is what tells those two apart. Only then DROP this patch rather than
refreshing it.
```

## 0018-ggml-amx-free-the-aligned-buffer.patch

**Files (1):** `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/amx/amx.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu(amx): free the AMX weight buffer with ggml_aligned_free(), not free()

ggml_backend_amx_buffer_type_alloc_buffer() allocates the buffer that holds the AMX-repacked
weights with ggml_aligned_malloc(), and ggml_backend_amx_buffer_free_buffer() releases it with
free(). On Linux that pair is fine (posix_memalign memory is free()-able). On Windows
ggml_aligned_malloc() is _aligned_malloc(), whose memory only _aligned_free() may release: free()
on it corrupts the CRT heap, and the process dies with STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION (0xC0000374) the
moment the model is unloaded -- after inference worked. The CPU buffer type next to it already
does it right (ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_free_buffer -> ggml_aligned_free), and ggml_aligned_free()
is free() on Linux, so nothing changes there.

Reached by: a Windows build whose chosen CPU module carries AMX (GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS ->
ggml-cpu-sapphirerapids, which ggml_backend_load_best() picks on Sapphire, Emerald and Granite
Rapids; ggml_amx_init() returns true unconditionally on _WIN32) and a model with weight types that
have AMX kernels (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q8_0, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, IQ4_XS). Found by java-llama.cpp's Publish
run 38069595101 (2026-10-10): the Windows x86-64 Java test job landed on an "Intel(R) Xeon(R)
6973P-C" runner (Granite Rapids), loaded ggml-cpu-sapphirerapids.dll, ran two generations on
Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-Q4_K_M, and the fork died with exit code -1073740940 (0xC0000374) at the
model's close(); the same job was green an hour earlier (run 38065017595) on an AMD EPYC 7763
runner, which has no AVX-512 and loads the haswell module. Upstream master still had the free()
on 2026-10-10. Not yet reported upstream (nothing is filed before this project's release).

Every other caller of ggml_aligned_malloc() in the tree pairs it correctly -- ggml-backend.cpp,
ggml-cpu.c (twice), ggml-openvino.cpp, ggml-zdnn.cpp and ggml.c itself -- so this was the one
mismatched pair, and ggml-backend.cpp:2464 is the line this fix copies.

Reproduced deliberately afterwards, rather than waiting for CI to draw AMX hardware again: on a
rented Granite Rapids machine, one CPU backend module staged at a time, same model, same binaries:

    module            runs  exit
    sapphirerapids       6   -1073740940 (0xC0000374)   <- the only module with the AMX path
    cooperlake           2   0
    icelake              2   0
    haswell              2   0

The same six runs on Linux with the same CPU all exit 0 with byte-identical output. It reproduces at
one thread, so it is not a data race, and the crash lands after the inference has printed its
timings -- the signature of a heap corrupted earlier and detected at free. With this patch applied,
the identical matrix on the same machine gives exit 0 in all twelve runs.

Guard on the downstream side: llama/cmake/check-aligned-free-pairing.cmake fails the configure on
any platform when a ggml source calls ggml_aligned_malloc() and never ggml_aligned_free(). A
run-time test cannot replace it -- without an AMX CPU there is nothing to observe, which is exactly
how this shipped.

Drop this patch when upstream frees the AMX buffer with ggml_aligned_free() or _aligned_free():
grep "free(buffer->context)" ggml/src/ggml-cpu/amx/amx.cpp at the new tag. NOTE THE INVERSION --
a hit means the bare free() is STILL THERE and this patch is still needed; it is droppable when the
grep prints NOTHING. Measured at b11639 (a0e6dc738): one hit, line 46, so the defect stands.
```

## 0020-ggml-alloc-validate-leafs-before-reusing-an-allocation.patch

**Files (1):** `ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-alloc : validate the leafs before reusing a graph's allocation

ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph() assigns every tensor of a graph by position from the previous
ggml_gallocr_reserve(): node i takes node_allocs[i], leaf i takes leaf_allocs[i].
ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc() decides whether those assignments still fit, and it validates every
node and every node's sources -- but of the leafs it compares only the count. A graph with the
same number of leafs in another order therefore reuses the old leaf assignments: an input leaf
lands on a slot that belonged to a weight (buffer_id -1, nothing allocated), and with NDEBUG the
asserts in ggml_gallocr_init_tensor() are gone, so ggml_vbuffer_tensor_alloc() indexes
galloc->buffers[-1]. A leaf that lands on a slot of another input is not caught either: its size
is never checked, so it may get a region too small for it.

Reached since #30445 ("graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings", cb55ffe6e, b11574..b11612):
the models no longer expand their LM head themselves, build_logits() does, after build_pooling().
In a context with embeddings enabled the reserved graph expands t_embd first and t_logits
second; a generation step on the same context (the server switches embeddings off for a slot
that samples, llama_set_embeddings(ctx, false)) expands only t_logits, whose first source is
output.weight. Same node and leaf counts, every leaf after output.weight shifted by one. Found
by java-llama.cpp's Publish run 38648257387 (2026-10-14): ErrorHandlingTest loads its model with
--embedding and posts an infill request to it, and the forked JVM died with SIGSEGV in
ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph on Linux, and with 0xC0000005 under both Windows toolchains:

    ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph <- ggml_backend_sched_alloc_graph <- llama_context::process_ubatch
    <- llama_context::decode <- server_context_impl::update_slots

Reproduced locally with a random 2-layer llama GGUF (FIM tokens set) and a context of 128:
infill on the model without --embedding works, with --embedding it crashes; a debug print shows
leaf 31 'out_ids' arriving at a slot with no allocation. Reverting cb55ffe6e makes it pass, and
so does this patch, which validates the leafs exactly as the nodes are validated: an invalid
leaf makes the allocator reserve again (one buffer) or report false, on which
ggml_backend_sched reserves the graph itself. With it, greedy infill on the --embedding model
returns the same tokens as on the model without, run after run.

The guard is src/test/cpp/test_gallocr_leafs.cpp: two graphs with the same nodes in the same order
and only the leafs moved (it dies with SIGSEGV without this patch), reserve with one, allocate the other.

Drop-check on every bump: read ggml_gallocr_needs_realloc() in ggml/src/ggml-alloc.c at the new
tag -- once it walks graph->leafs itself, drop this patch rather than refreshing it.
```

## 0021-server-a-slot-file-carries-the-lora-config-its-state-was-computed-with.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server-context.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server : a slot file carries the LoRA config its state was computed with

Since upstream #32434 (b12498) a slot's prompt carries the LoRA config its tokens were processed
with (server_prompt::lora): launch_slot_with_task() compares a task's adapters with it, the
host-memory prompt cache stores it with every state and skips the states of another config. A slot
file does not store it (upstream's TODO in server-slot-sched.h), and SLOT_RESTORE leaves
prompt.lora as it was -- empty in a never-used slot. On a server started with --lora the first
task then read the restored state as "computed under no adapters" and cleared it (F240: 77 of 79
prompt tokens evaluated again), and in a slot that had served a task under other adapters the
restored state kept that slot's label.

The patch appends the config to the slot file, after the checkpoints and the draft state, as a
section of its own ("SLRA", version 1: per adapter its path and its scale), and a restore labels the
state with it on the adapters loaded at that time, matched by path; an adapter the section does not
name has scale 0. A state computed under no adapters writes no section, and a file without one --
upstream's format, or one saved by a server without adapters -- counts as computed under none, which
is what upstream assumes for a never-used slot: the first task with adapters clears it. A section
that cannot be read, data after the state that no section reads (a checkpoint or draft section that
could not be read -- cut, or of another version -- behind which the config may lie), or a section
that names an adapter at a scale other than 0 which this server has not loaded, refuses the restore
(invalid request) and leaves the slot empty: no task of this server computes under that config, and
"none" for an unknown config would reuse a state computed with adapters on a server without any.
Upstream's reader ignores what follows its sections, so upstream reads these files as before. Not
reset by a refused restore: the speculative state a draft section set, as upstream's SLOT_ERASE
leaves it too.

Only the scales and paths are stored, never the adapter infos: a wake from the idle sleep frees the
adapters and loads them again, and a stored info would carry a pointer into freed memory
(are_lora_equal compares the pointers, lora_should_clear_cache reads through them).

History: until the review of 2026-11-19 the patch kept the scales of every file the server saved in
a map by path, so a file of an earlier process, or a copy under another name, counted as computed
under none; in the first round of the review of 2026-11-18 it stored the adapter infos themselves
(pointers that a sleep frees); before it, it labelled a restored state with the server's adapters at
the time of the restore, which reused a state saved under scale 1 after setLoraAdapters() had set
scale 0; until b12497 it started every slot with slot.lora = params_base.lora_adapters in init(),
which upstream's comparison no longer reads.

The guard is src/test/cpp/test_lora_cache.cpp: its LoraCacheFreshSlot fixture restores slot 0's
saved state into the never-used slot 1, which must reuse it; restores a state saved under other
scales, which may not be reused, and a copy of a file under another name, which may; and refuses a
truncated section. LoraCacheFiles restores a file into a model loaded again, which must reuse it,
refuses it in a model without the adapter, restores a file saved without adapters, which the first
task clears, and refuses a file whose draft section was cut (the section behind it lost);
LoraCacheSleep restores a state after the model slept, which must be reused. The other cases hold
upstream's half.

Drop-check on every bump: read the SLOT_SAVE and SLOT_RESTORE cases in
tools/server/server-context.cpp at the new tag -- once the slot file stores the LoRA config and the
restore sets prompt.lora from it, drop the patch; if upstream stores it in another form, a file
written by this patch is still read by upstream (it ignores the trailing section).
```

## 0022-ggml-cpu-repack-batch-the-tokens-of-an-expert.patch

**Files (3):** `ggml/include/ggml-cpu.h`, `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.cpp`, `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu : batch the tokens of an expert in the repack MUL_MAT_ID, and hand its work out dynamically

forward_mul_mat_id() of the CPU_REPACK buffer (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp) runs the expert
matmuls of every MoE model whose expert weights are repacked at load -- MXFP4 (gpt-oss), Q4_0,
IQ4_NL and Q4_K on AVX2, and their interleaved forms on ARM -- and it pays two costs that
forward_mul_mat() of the same buffer does not:

1. One gemv per token. The tokens routed to an expert are multiplied one at a time, so the 4-bit
   weights are unpacked once per token, and the gemm kernel that exists for the same type is never
   reached from here. In ggml's generic MUL_MAT_ID the tiled kernels take over for batches, but they
   cover K-quants and IQ types, not MXFP4.
2. A static split. Thread ith gets the fixed rows [ith*n/nth, (ith+1)*n/nth) of every expert, so
   each expert matmul ends when the slowest thread does -- on a hybrid CPU, at the pace of its
   slowest core. forward_mul_mat() hands its chunks out through ggml_threadpool_chunk_add().

The patch keeps that path and adds a second one; thread 0 picks one per op, before the grouping
barrier, from a process-wide switch, and publishes the choice in the work buffer, so a flip during a
compute cannot send the threads down different paths:

  ggml_backend_cpu_set_repack_mmid_batched(bool) / ggml_backend_cpu_get_repack_mmid_batched()
  (ggml-cpu.h, and in the CPU backend's get_proc_address table for a GGML_BACKEND_DL build).
  On by default; GGML_CPU_REPACK_MMID_BATCHED=0 in the environment makes off the initial value.

The batched path: thread 0 lists the experts that got rows and where each one's groups of four
tokens start in a shared buffer. Every such group is gathered from src1 and quantized interleaved
with ggml_quantize_mat_t() -- the quantizer forward_mul_mat() uses for its gemm rows -- once, the
groups split statically over the threads, then a barrier (both skipped when no expert got four
tokens, as in token generation). The work is then (expert, column chunk) units, about 16 per
thread, taken through ggml_threadpool_chunk_add(); a unit multiplies up to 16 of the expert's
shared rows at a time with gemm() into a per-thread tile and scatters them back to the token rows,
and fewer than four leftover tokens take the gemv path from the rows quantized before.
work_size() reserves the per-op state, the shared rows (one per routed token slot; 6.3 MB for
gpt-oss-20b at a 512-token batch) and the per-thread scratch (four float rows and a 16-row output
tile) whatever the switch says, since it may flip before the graph runs.

Quantizing once matters where the activation quantizer is slow: ARM has no SIMD form of
ggml_quantize_mat_q8_K_4x4/4x8 (x86 has one for 4x8), and a first version of this patch, which
quantized an expert's rows again in every column chunk, made Q4_K prompt processing on a
Neoverse-N1 18 % slower at 32 threads (perf: 21 % of the time in the inlined generic quantizer).

Measured in java-llama.cpp (docs/benchmarks/moe-mxfp4-cpu-alderlake.md): a random-weight GGUF in
gpt-oss-20b's exact shape and ggml-org's MXFP4 layout, the alderlake CPU module (AVX2 + AVX-VNNI)
staged alone, 4 threads: prompt processing +46 % (43.9 -> 64.1 t/s), token generation +23 %
(7.84 -> 9.63 t/s), single-threaded prompt processing +59 %; the barrier wait after MUL_MAT_ID
fell from 13.9 % to 1.7 % of all thread time. llama-perplexity with --kl-divergence against the
unchanged code: mean KLD 0.000000, max 0.000002, same top token 100 %.

With real weights (b11901, llama-bench pp512, switch off -> on, t/s;
docs/benchmarks/moe-repack-real-weights.md): a Ryzen 7 5800H (Zen 3, haswell module), 8 threads,
gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 41.7 -> 59.6, Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M 58.3 -> 84.7, OLMoE-1B-7B Q4_0
138.8 -> 190.0; a Neoverse-N1 (dotprod, armv8.2_2 module), 32 threads, 177.0 -> 278.7,
190.7 -> 215.7 and 705.9 -> 990.0; an IBM z16 (z16 module, big-endian OLMoE Q4_0), 4 threads,
45.8 -> 76.2. Token generation is unchanged within noise. KLD against the unchanged code on
wikitext-2: 0.000000 for MXFP4 and Q4_0 (same top token 100 %, 99.98 % on the z16); 0.0075 for
Q4_K, where the gemm and gemv kernels round
differently and a router flips experts on near ties -- upstream's repack path is as far from
--no-repack (0.0080 on the N1) as the batched one (0.0085).

The switch is this project's addition, for A/B measurements on a user's own machine
(LlamaModel.setCpuMoeBatched, jllama_set_cpu_moe_batched, the environment variable); an upstream
submission would offer the batched path alone.

The guard is src/test/cpp/test_moe_repack.cpp: MUL_MAT_ID over repacked weights of four types, with
both settings of the switch and 1, 3 and 4 threads, against the generic path over the same weights
in a plain buffer, for routings that give an expert 0, 1, 3, 4 and 17 tokens, a slot of -1, one
token alone and one input row per slot; and the switch is resolved through the CPU backend's
get_proc_address, so a bump that drops the patch reds the test at once.

Drop-check on every bump: read forward_mul_mat_id() in ggml/src/ggml-cpu/repack.cpp at the new tag
-- once upstream calls gemm for an expert's batched rows and hands the work out through
ggml_threadpool_chunk_add(), drop this patch (and with it the switch) rather than refreshing it.
```

## 0023-ggml-cpu-s390x-variants-build-with-clang-and-a-z13-baseline.patch

**Files (3):** `ggml/src/CMakeLists.txt`, `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt`, `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/llamafile/sgemm.h`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
ggml-cpu(s390x): CPU variants that build with clang, and a scalar z13 baseline

GGML_CPU_ALL_VARIANTS builds the IBM Z modules ggml-cpu-z15 (VXE2) and ggml-cpu-z16 (VXE2 + NNPA)
with -march=z15/z16 -mvx -mzvector. Two things stand between that list and a jar that runs on
every machine the scalar library runs on today.

1. With clang, every translation unit that includes both ggml-cpu-impl.h and llamafile/sgemm.h
   fails: both include <vecintrin.h> under `defined(__VXE__) || defined(__VXE2__)`, and clang's
   vecintrin.h has no include guard (GCC's has _VECINTRIN_H), so the second inclusion redefines
   vec_extract, vec_insert and the rest ("redefinition of 'vec_extract'", first in ggml-cpu.c,
   which includes ggml-cpu-impl.h at line 7 and llamafile/sgemm.h at line 51). Nothing in the
   object code is duplicated; it is a compile error. The include in sgemm.h came with
   ggml-org/llama.cpp#14273 ("llamafile : support s390x SIMD instruction set", 2025-06-19), and it
   is not needed: sgemm.h declares no vector type, and both files that include it include
   ggml-cpu-impl.h as well -- sgemm.cpp right after it (where __VXE__ is not defined yet, because
   ggml-cpu-impl.h is what defines it from __VEC__, so the include there never fired), ggml-cpu.c
   before it (where it is the duplicate). Upstream documents GCC as the s390x compiler
   (docs/build-s390x.md), which is why it went unnoticed. This patch removes the include from
   sgemm.h; ggml-cpu-impl.h keeps the one that is used.

2. The list starts at z15, so a machine without VXE2 (z13, z14) would find no CPU backend at all,
   where the scalar build ran. The patch adds ggml-cpu-z13: no VXE, -march=z13 (the range of the
   cross-compile flags starts at 13 for it), score 1 in arch/s390/cpu-feats.cpp, so
   ggml_backend_load_best() takes it only where z15 and z16 score 0. z13 is the oldest machine
   RHEL 8, SLES 15 and Ubuntu support, and the floor java-llama.cpp's s390x jar has had.

z17 (-march=arch15) stays as upstream has it: added only when the compiler accepts the flag
(GCC 15.1, newer clang); clang 18 and 19 do not, and the configure skips it.

Measured on cfarm191 (IBM z16, LinuxONE, machine 3932, 8 IFLs shared, Debian 13, clang 19.1.7)
at b11901 with this patch, Qwen3-0.6B Q4_K_M converted to big-endian with gguf_convert_endian.py,
`llama-bench -t 4 -p 64 -n 16 -r 2`, two interleaved rounds, t/s:

    module                 pp64          tg16
    z13 (scalar)           19.7 - 19.8   13.6 - 13.8
    z15                    90.0 - 95.5   57.3 - 58.3
    z16                    82.6 - 88.3   51.9 - 53.9
    z16, GCC 14.2 (unpatched, for comparison)
                           85.2 - 86.4   44.1 - 53.9

With all three modules ggml loaded z16, without it z15, without both z13. Greedy output of
llama-simple is byte-identical between z15 and z16. Against z13 (llama-perplexity --kl-divergence,
9 chunks of 256 tokens) the vector modules differ by a mean KLD of 0.0087 (same top token 94.8 %) --
rounding, not a defect: against a Q8_0 reference computed on z13, the Q4_K_M model lands at a mean
KLD of 0.0777 on z13 and 0.0746 on z16 -- equally far from it, and the 0.0087 between them is about
a tenth of what the quantization itself costs. Q8_0 itself, z16 against z13: mean KLD 0.0012, same
top token 98.5 %.

Not filed upstream yet (nothing is filed before the owner says so).
```

## 0024-common-fs-is-directory-reads-utf8.patch

**Files (1):** `common/common.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
common: read the directory of --slot-save-path and --media-path as UTF-8 on Windows

fs_is_directory() (common/common.cpp:944 at b12242) builds the std::filesystem::path it checks from
the narrow std::string. MSVC's path constructor decodes a narrow string in the process's active
code page, and since b12131/b12132 nothing converts the argument first. The argument is UTF-8 (the
C API, and Java through JNI, pass UTF-8 on every platform), so on a code page like 1252 a directory
outside ASCII does not exist under the decoded name: c3 a4 (a-umlaut) is read as "A-tilde,
currency sign", e6 97 a5 (U+65E5) as three cp1252 characters. The two callers throw
"not a directory: <path>" (common/arg.cpp:3647 for --slot-save-path, :3661 for --media-path), and
the model load fails before anything is written. Upstream's own executables do not see it: they
carry an activeCodePage=UTF-8 manifest (common/win-app.manifest), and a library loaded into
java.exe cannot.

The fix reads the string as UTF-8 through std::filesystem::u8path(), which is the identity on
platforms whose narrow encoding is UTF-8 already.

Measured on 2026-11-10 (Windows 11, MSVC 19.44, GetACP() 1252, a directory "d-<a-umlaut>-<U+65E5>"):
without the patch the load is refused with "not a directory"; with it, a slot round-trips without a
draft model (n_written 9348 = size on disk = n_read). With a draft model the save still fails,
"Unable to save slot: incomplete draft state": the appendix is the subject of 0025, and only the two
together give the round trip. In a process with an activeCodePage=UTF-8 manifest the unpatched
check passes. See docs/handover/local-agent-report-windows-non-ascii-paths.md.

Drop-check: drop this patch when fs_is_directory() reads its argument as UTF-8 again (u8path, or a
wide conversion) -- CApiSlotFiles.ASlotDirectoryWithNonAsciiCharactersHoldsTheWholeSlotFile then
stays green without it on a Windows job.
```

## 0025-server-slot-appendix-reads-utf8.patch

**Files (1):** `tools/server/server-context.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
server: open the slot file's checkpoint and draft-state appendix as UTF-8 on Windows

A slot save writes the llama state through llama_state_seq_save_file(), i.e. ggml_fopen(), which
converts the UTF-8 path to UTF-16. Then save_slot_checkpoints() and save_slot_draft() append to the
same file through std::ofstream(filepath, binary | app), and load_slot_checkpoints() and
load_slot_draft() read it back through std::ifstream(filepath, binary | ate)
(tools/server/server-context.cpp:2840, :2872, :2948 and :2974 at b12242). MSVC decodes that narrow
std::string in the process's active code page, so on a code page like 1252 the appendix of a path
outside ASCII goes elsewhere:

  - a directory outside ASCII (once 0024 lets it through): the mis-decoded directory does not exist,
    the stream fails and the save reports "Unable to save slot: incomplete draft state". The
    9348-byte state without the appendix stays behind, and a restore of it succeeds without the
    draft state.
  - an ASCII directory with a file name outside ASCII (no other patch involved): the appendix lands
    in a second file under the mis-decoded name, next to the real one. Measured:
    "f-<a-umlaut>-<U+65E5>-draft.bin" 9348 bytes plus its mangled twin 9216 bytes. The save reports
    ok with n_written 18564, the sum of both files; the restore reports ok with n_read 9348, and the
    draft state is silently gone.

The fix opens the four streams on std::filesystem::u8path(filepath), which is the identity where the
narrow encoding is UTF-8.

Measured on 2026-11-10 (Windows 11, MSVC 19.44, GetACP() 1252, tiny llama model with itself as the
draft model, --spec-type draft-simple): with 0024 and this patch both shapes round-trip, with a single
18564-byte file each, n_written = size on disk = n_read, and n_restored = n_saved. The checkpoint
appendix shares these sites but is not exercised by the tiny model (no checkpoints): read, not
measured. See docs/handover/local-agent-report-windows-non-ascii-paths.md.

Drop-check: drop this patch when the four streams in server-context.cpp no longer take the narrow
filepath string -- CApiSlotFiles.ASlotFileNameWithNonAsciiCharactersIsOneFileThatRestoresWhole then
stays green without it on a Windows job.
```

## 0030-common-arg-env-reads-utf8.patch

**Files (1):** `common/arg.cpp`

The patch's own header, verbatim:

```text
common: read an option's environment variable as UTF-8 on Windows

common_arg::get_value_from_env() (common/arg.cpp:114 at b12283) takes an option's value from
std::getenv(), which on Windows answers in the process's active code page. Every handler reads its
value as UTF-8 -- the same handler serves the command line, which the C API and Java pass as UTF-8
-- and since 0024 to 0029 the paths behind them are opened as UTF-8 too. So inside java.exe on a
code page like 1252 a LLAMA_ARG_SLOT_SAVE_PATH, LLAMA_ARG_LOG_FILE or LLAMA_ARG_MODEL outside ASCII
named another string than the same value as an argument: the directory check failed and the model
did not load. The environment is applied before the arguments, so an argument that would have
overridden the variable did not help: the load had already failed on it. Upstream's own
executables do not see it: they carry an activeCodePage=UTF-8 manifest, and a library loaded into
java.exe cannot.

The fix reads the variable with _wgetenv() and converts it to UTF-8 (through
std::filesystem::path, so no <windows.h> in this file); elsewhere it is std::getenv() as before.
It covers every option with an environment variable, not only the paths: a value is text either
way.

Found by the review of PR #612; measured on Windows 11, code page 1252, on 2026-11-11
(docs/handover/local-agent-report-windows-non-ascii-paths-b12283.md): red without the patch,
green with it.

on Windows -- CApiNonAsciiPaths.AnOptionFromTheEnvironmentIsReadAsUtf8 then stays green without it
```
